item.title: Asking Good Questions and Planning an Analysis
item.description: Lesson 2: Asking Good Questions and Planning an Analysis A good analysis is decided before a single chart is drawn. item.title: Finding, Cleaning, and Preparing Data You Can Trust

item.title: Describing Data — Summaries, Distributions, and What "Average" Hides
item.description: Lesson 4: Describing Data — Summaries, Distributions, and What "Average" Hides Before hunting for complex patterns, describe your data plainly. Descriptive analysis answers: what does this data look like, what is typical, how much does it vary, and are there unusual values? These simple summaries…

item.description: Lesson 5: Exploring Patterns — Comparisons, Trends, and Relationships Once you can describe data, you can explore it: compare groups, follow trends over time, and examine relationships between variables. item.description: Lesson 6: Testing Ideas and Avoiding False Conclusions Exploration suggests ideas; testing checks them. You do not need advanced statistics to test an idea well.
